Mass drug administration (MDA) is a strategy that involves administering antischistosomal drugs to large populations to eliminate a parasite. While MDA has been effective in controlling schistosomiasis, which is a parasitic infection caused by Schistosoma parasites, its sustainability depends on several factors.

MDA on its own was not sufficient to control the prevalence of schistosomiasis, intensity of infection, or morbidity of the disease. Alternative control measures will be needed to complement the existing national MDA program.

In other words, while mass drug administration is an effective tool for controlling schistosomiasis, it requires careful consideration and planning to ensure its sustainability in a population.
